name: Scree Slope
desc: A cliff shatters itself into the apron below it — freeze-thaw pries blocks off the exposed face in bursts, they run down the couloirs and come to rest where the slope slackens, so talus cones splay out and the clasts fall-sort coarse toward the toe; the massif keeps rising and a stream keeps eating the foot of the pile, so the face never retreats to rest.

energy.doc: shattering vigour + uplift rate + colour/contrast gain

scale.doc: magnification into the slope around x/y — 1 shows cliff and apron, 2.6 crops to a single cone

speed.doc: rate of weathering, rockfall and cliff retreat

density.doc: rockfall frequency — an occasional clatter at 0, a continuous shedding face at 1

repose.doc: angle of repose: 0 = fine debris spreading into a low flat apron, 1 = coarse blocks stacking into steep cones

hue.doc: rock hue anchor; rotates the plate with it

x.doc: view centre x (only bites when scale > 1)

y.doc: view centre y (only bites when scale > 1)

style.doc: aesthetic: survey = bedded ochre cliff over cool grey-violet talus, clasts reading coarse at the toe; hypsometric = false-colour elevation ramp + hillshade relief plate; silver = chiaroscuro, form from light only, no colour and no outline; ink = sumi tonal wash
